sb_prompt: DO YOU BELIEVE THAT THE US GOVERNMENT SHOULD PROVIDE UNIVERSAL HEALTH INSURANCE
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: Can I ask you something real quick?
ParticipantB: Sure, what's up?
ParticipantA: I'm trying to figure out if you think the US government should do universal health insurance.
ParticipantB: Oh, yeah. That's a big question.
ParticipantA: Tell me why you think that way.
ParticipantB: Well, honestly, I think they should. Look, I'm a nurse, you know?
ParticipantA: Right, I'm a real estate agent.
ParticipantB: Yeah, and working in the hospital... it's just crazy.
ParticipantA: Tell me about it.
ParticipantB: Like last week, I had a patient come in with a broken leg. He fell at work.
ParticipantA: Oh, really?
ParticipantB: His insurance company said, "No, we don't cover that kind of injury," so we had to find a place that would take him even though he didn't have coverage.
ParticipantA: That sucks.
ParticipantB: It does. He was in pain, he needed the cast, he needed the follow-ups. If he didn't get it, he'd lose his job, he'd lose his apartment.
ParticipantA: Man, that is rough. I know my cousin got into a car accident a few years ago.
ParticipantB: Oh?
ParticipantA: Yeah, he was driving and hit a tree. He had to stay in the hospital for a week.
ParticipantB: How'd he handle the cost?
ParticipantA: Well, he had insurance, so it was mostly covered. But the deductible was like three thousand dollars.
ParticipantB: Three thousand?!
ParticipantA: Yeah. That was a blow to his savings. But he was okay.
ParticipantB: If that guy didn't have insurance, what would happen?
ParticipantA: Well, he couldn't afford it. He'd have to choose between paying for the leg and paying rent.
ParticipantB: Exactly. That's the problem. People are dying because they can't afford basic stuff.
ParticipantA: Hmm. I guess you're right. I've seen people in my listings who are terrified of getting sick.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it's scary.
ParticipantA: Do you think the government could actually pay for it?
ParticipantB: I don't know. My boss says it would bankrupt the country.
ParticipantA: Really?
ParticipantB: Yeah. He says taxes would go up so much people would revolt. And we'd have to hire more doctors, more nurses, more equipment.
ParticipantA: That sounds expensive.
ParticipantB: But he's never seen a patient go bankrupt just because he got sick.
ParticipantA: Hmm. That's a good point. I'm usually worried about taxes, though.
ParticipantB: So you'd rather people just pay for it themselves?
ParticipantA: Not really. I'd rather it was shared. Like, maybe not everyone gets the same thing, but no one gets shut out.
ParticipantB: I agree with that.
ParticipantA: What about you? Do you think everyone should get the exact same plan?
ParticipantB: No, I think everyone should have access to what they need. If I'm sick, I should get treated. If you're sick, you should get treated. It shouldn't depend on your job.
ParticipantA: That makes sense to me. My cousin had that scare, and now he's saving extra just in case.
ParticipantB: It's stressful.
ParticipantA: Yeah. Do you think it could work?
ParticipantB: I think it could. If we fix the system first. Right now it's just a mess.
ParticipantA: I agree. It's a mess.
ParticipantB: Yeah.
ParticipantA: Well, I guess I'll keep thinking about it. Thanks for talking to me.
ParticipantB: Yeah, same here. Good luck.
ParticipantA: Bye.
ParticipantB: Bye.
